God gave humans free will. You can't use him as an excuse for your own lack of discipline and morals.

The conundrum is called theodicy. The problem is that many of the attempts to define the attributes of God in the major monotheistic religions involve mutually exclusive descriptions. 'All powerful', 'all good' and 'all knowing' make the idea of free will nothing but a verbal illusion. If God is all knowing it means he knows in advance the choice of every act of free will ie that the course of the universe is rigidly determined. If he is all good then he should do all in his power to prevent any instance of evil including those that result from the 'free will' choices whose outcome he already knows. If he is all powerful then he can damn well act and correct each and every evil outcome.

This leaves 'free will' as an impossibility and a verbal charade if one wishes to retain the other descriptors. The only escape is to "pull the Joker from the deck" and throw these problems into the "mystery of God" stewpot.

Yet again, we have a Dan Henry watch to unbox. After really loving the 1939 and 1963 models,I decided to go backward in time and purchase the 1947.

Included in the plastic tube package is a canvas and leather 3-watch roll containing the watch itself (on a nice crocodile-pattern Italian leather strap), a one-year warranty card and a black military-grade NATO strap (which I don't see myself using very often, as this watch is a tad too dressy for it).

The specs of the watch are as follows:

CASE

  • 40mm stainless steel 316L
  • 22mm lugs size 47.8mm lug to lug
  • Screw-back case with 3D Maze
  • Sapphire coated double domed mineral glass with Anti-Reflective treatment

MOVEMENT

  • Seiko VD78 quartz (Japan)

DIAL

  • Brushed chapter ring with rose gold applied roman numerals and indexes
  • Rose gold Leaf-shaped hands
  • Silver Guilloché subdial with blue hands

The first thing you notice about the 1947 (especially if you are an OMEGA aficionado) is the fact that, except for size, it looks just like an OMEGA Chronometer ref. 2366. I mean, just like it. That's an old-ass watch, though, so that fact coupled with how well-made this dial is made it possible to forgive Mr. Henry at once.

This dial is superb. It is one of the nicest, best-finished dials that I have seen at any price (that may be new-watch hyperbole, but not by much). It is matte-silver with light texturing with a fairly thick ring of brushed silver that is home to the gorgeous rose-gold Arabic numbers and markers.

The rose-gold (coloured) leaf hands are also a holdover from OMEGA, so they are unsurprisingly right at home on this watch. All of the rose-gold (I'm not a fan of too much gold, this watch gets it just right) applications look flawless and I'm really happy that I went with the gold version.

Moving out from the brushed circle, the is a gap of a couple of centimetres followed by a ring of minute-markers (again, huzzah, OMEGA!). The seconds hand subdial is beneath the main dial with a polished, beveled edge and a blue hand.

Moving on from the dial, we come to the case. In appearance, it seems to be influenced by the likes of Patek Philippe and Vacheron Constantin. It is a simple, pleasing barrel-shaped case, all brushed except for the side of the bezel, which is polished. There is a maze etched onto the caseback for reasons I cannot fathom, but it looks cool (stolen from the website as I forgot to photograph it). Also, as this is a "limited edition," the watch is numbered. I got 0086/1947. All of this is done so very nicely that it's difficult to believe that this thing only costs $190. What a steal.

Dan Henry watches take special care with attention to detail. The crown and buckles are signed, the seconds hand hits the tic-marks perfectly, the brushed areas don't intrude upon the polished bits. Things that one "just expects" at a certain price-point simply don't happen with this brand (SEIKO, you can put a bezel on straight, you know you can).

The included croc-pattern leather strap is quite nice and I'll keep it on this watch for the foreseeable future.

The movement is a SEIKO VD78 quartz movement that will likely outlive me.

As if you cannot tell, I am smitten with this brand, quartz be damned. Dan Henry's offerings have quality and a level of detail not typically found in watches this inexpensive. I am super-happy with the three I've got.

Well, I'm sure we'll meet again when I buy the 1968 or 1970.
